title: feat!: replace polars dependency with arrow; bump to 0.3.0
description:
## Summary

- Upgrades to ggsql Rust crate v0.3.0 and bumps the Python package version to 0.3.0
- Rewrites the Rust↔Python IPC bridge to use Arrow directly instead of Polars, matching the upstream ggsql v0.3.0 change that removed Polars from the crate
- Rust side uses `arrow::ipc::{StreamWriter, StreamReader}` and Python side uses `pyarrow.ipc`
- Runtime dependency changed from `polars` to `pyarrow`
- Custom readers returning Polars DataFrames still work — `py_to_df()` accepts anything `pyarrow.table()` can convert
- Adds `build.rs` to link `rstrtmgr.lib` on Windows (required by DuckDB 1.4+)
- Updates README, CLAUDE.md, CHANGELOG, and tests to reflect the new Arrow-based API

### Public API changes

- `DuckDBReader.execute_sql()` returns `pyarrow.Table` (was `polars.DataFrame`)
- `DuckDBReader.register()` accepts `pyarrow.Table` (polars/pandas also accepted via automatic conversion)
- `Spec.data()` / `layer_data()` / `stat_data()` return `pyarrow.Table`

## Test plan

- [x] All 45 tests pass locally (2 skipped: pandas, ibis not installed)
- [ ] CI passes across platforms (Linux, macOS, Windows) and Python versions (3.10–3.13)

title: port over changes from posit-dev/ggsql#178
description:
# From posit-dev/ggsql#178

## Summary
- Add typed exception classes (`ParseError`, `ValidationError`, `ReaderError`, `WriterError`) subclassing `ValueError` for backwards compatibility
- Add `Reader` protocol class defining the contract for custom readers (`execute_sql`, `register`)
- Fix `PyReaderBridge` to pass `replace` as a keyword argument, so custom readers with `register(name, df, *, replace=False)` signatures work correctly

## Rust changes
- `create_exception!` macros for 4 exception types + `ggsql_err_to_py()` mapper
- All `.map_err(...)` sites updated from generic `PyValueError` to typed exceptions
- `PyReaderBridge.register()` uses `call_method` with kwargs instead of `call_method1`

# From posit-dev/ggsql#179

## Summary
- Add type stubs (`.pyi`) for the native `_ggsql` extension module, enabling IDE autocompletion and type checking
- Add `data=` dict parameter on `execute()` for registering temporary DataFrames that are automatically cleaned up after execution (even on error)
- Improve type stub specificity and data cleanup safety

## Rust changes
- `data: Option<&Bound<'_, PyDict>>` parameter on `PyDuckDBReader.execute()` and free `execute()`
- `register_data_dict()` / `register_data_on_reader()` helpers with `table_exists()` probe to avoid unregistering pre-existing tables
- Removed `try_native_readers!` macro (incompatible with cleanup-before-return pattern)

title: feat: upgrade to ggsql 0.5.2 with native SVG/PDF/HEP writers
description:
## Summary

Upgrades the Python bindings from ggsql Rust crate v0.3.3 to **v0.5.2**, and exposes the crate's new native rendering capabilities in Python. Upstream 0.4.0–0.5.2 brings many ggsql language and rendering improvements — see the [crate changelog](https://github.com/posit-dev/ggsql/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) for details.

High-level impact:

- **Native rendering, no JavaScript**: new `SVGWriter`, `PDFWriter`, and `HepWriter` classes render `Spec`s directly via ggsql's native renderer (hephaestus). `render()` returns `str` (SVG) or `bytes` (PDF/HEP), and render warnings are surfaced via `warnings.warn()`.
- **One-call file export**: new `ggsql.save(spec, file, ...)` helper picks the writer from the file extension (`.svg`, `.pdf`, `.hep`, or `.json` for Vega-Lite).
- **Builtin datasets**: the crate's `builtin-data` feature is enabled, so queries can reference datasets like `ggsql:world`.
- **Explicit chart kwargs**: `VegaLiteWriter.render_chart()` and `render_altair()` now accept `validate`, `height`, and `width` as keyword arguments (`height`/`width` default to `None`, preserving ggsql's dimensions; `validate` defaults to `False`, same behavior as before).
- **Dependency bumps**: Arrow v56 → v58; Python package version bumped to 0.5.2 to match the crate.

Also documents the `py/v*` release-tag workflow in `CLAUDE.md`.

### Note: vendored ggsql patch (temporary)

Bundled duckdb builds fail on Windows/MSVC with ggsql 0.5.2's pinned `duckdb ~1.10502`: duckdb 1.5.2's vendored fmt uses `stdext::checked_array_iterator` (removed from current MSVC STL) under `#ifdef _SECURE_SCL`. This was fixed upstream in libduckdb-sys 1.10506.0 ([duckdb/duckdb-rs#783](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb-rs/pull/783)), so this PR temporarily vendors ggsql 0.5.2 via `[patch.crates-io]` with the pin relaxed to `~1.10506` (see `vendor/ggsql/`). The only change to the vendored crate is that one-line version relaxation, marked with a `PATCHED` comment in its `Cargo.toml`. The vendor directory and `[patch]` section should be removed once a ggsql release depends on duckdb `~1.10506`.

## Verification

```python
import ggsql

reader = ggsql.DuckDBReader("duckdb://memory")
spec = reader.execute("SELECT 1 AS x, 2 AS y VISUALISE x, y DRAW point")

svg = ggsql.SVGWriter(width=600, height=400).render(spec)  # str
pdf = ggsql.PDFWriter(width=600, height=400).render(spec)  # bytes

ggsql.save(spec, "plot.svg")
ggsql.save(spec, "plot.pdf")
ggsql.save(spec, "plot.json")  # Vega-Lite JSON
```

Tests: `uv run pytest tests/ -v` (includes new coverage for the native writers, `save()`, and builtin datasets). Rust checks: `cargo fmt -- --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`.

title: Add CachingReader binding (stacked on #9)
description:
## Summary

Exposes upstream ggsql 0.5.2's `CachingReader` to Python as `ggsql.CachingReader`. Source reads hit the primary reader (memoized with TTL + LRU byte budget); all ggsql-generated derived SQL (`__ggsql_*` tables) runs on a private in-memory DuckDB cache.

```python
reader = ggsql.CachingReader("duckdb://memory", ttl_secs=60)
# or wrap any Python object with the bridge protocol
# (execute_sql / register / unregister) — the querychat path
reader = ggsql.CachingReader(my_reader)
spec = reader.execute("SELECT ... VISUALISE ...")
```

- Primary accepts a `duckdb://` connection string (built fresh internally) or a bridged Python reader; passing an existing `DuckDBReader` instance errors with guidance.
- Config from `GGSQL_CACHE_DISABLED` / `GGSQL_CACHE_TTL` / `GGSQL_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`, keyword args take precedence.
- No GIL release in `execute` (bridged primaries call back into Python — same stance as `DuckDBReader`).

**Why:** querychat currently rejects ggsql queries with layer-level sources and re-runs identical base reads on every LLM tool call. `test_layer_level_source_through_bridge` demonstrates `VISUALISE ... FROM <table>` running end-to-end through a bridged primary — the capability querychat's `_viz_ggsql.py` names as its long-term fix.

## Benchmark evidence (merge gate)

Benchmark: simulated LLM-style viz session — 9 tool calls sharing one identical base read over a 3M-row DataFrameSource (iterative chart refinement), 1 exact repeat, 1 multi-relation query. Old path = querychat's hand-rolled split (`_viz_ggsql.py` @ querychat 40f328e4); new path = whole-query execution through `CachingReader` wrapping the querychat executor — see draft PR [posit-dev/querychat#321](https://github.com/posit-dev/querychat/pull/321) for the integration.

| call | old (s) | new (s) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 4.839 | 5.107 |
| 2 | 5.909 | 3.576 |
| 3 | 7.512 | 5.322 |
| 4 | 5.335 | 2.979 |
| 5 | 4.459 | 2.195 |
| 6 | 5.947 | 3.684 |
| 7 | 5.256 | 2.981 |
| 8 | 5.922 | 3.623 |
| 9 | 5.896 | 3.647 |
| multi-relation | **unsupported** | 3.582s |
| **total (calls 1–9)** | **51.075** | **33.113** |

**Source reads during calls 1–9 (one shared base read): old = 9, new = 1.** The multi-relation call adds 2 more on the new path (base + layer source); the old path rejects such queries outright.

Takeaways:

- **9× fewer source reads** for iterative chart refinement — the LLM loop's dominant pattern.
- **~35% wall-time reduction** overall, with no cold-path regression (call 1: 5.1s vs 4.8s — small cache-staging overhead).
- Remaining per-call cost is data movement + Vega-Lite rendering of the ~1.5M-row result, not the source read.
- **Capability unlock:** `DRAW ... FROM <table>` (multi-relation) queries now work end-to-end through the bridged executor.

Environment: ggsql 0.5.2 (this branch), M-series arm64, Python 3.12. Two consecutive runs produced near-identical numbers. Repro: `.venv/bin/python _dev/ggsql-caching-benchmark/bench.py` on querychat branch `ggsql-caching-reader` ([posit-dev/querychat#321](https://github.com/posit-dev/querychat/pull/321)).

## Stacking

Stacked on #9 (`ggsql-0.5.2-upgrade`); base retargets to `main` after #9 merges. Design spec and implementation plan live locally in `docs/superpowers/` (gitignored).

## Test plan

- 15 new tests: constructor dispatch, memoization hit/miss, TTL expiry, `enabled=False` + env-var disable, layer-level source through bridged primary, cache-resident routing, top-level `execute` fast path, package export
- Full suite: 121 passed, 5 skipped; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` clean

title: feat: zero-copy Arrow C Data Interface at the Python/Rust boundary
description:
## Summary - Replaces Arrow IPC serialization with zero-copy Arrow C Data Interface (PyCapsule) transfers for all data crossing the Python↔Rust boundary. All nine call sites funnel through `py_to_df()`/`df_to_py()` in `src/lib.rs`, so there are no signature changes — those two functions are now dispatchers. - The legacy IPC path is retained behind `GGSQL_ARROW_IPC=1` as an escape hatch (e.g., for exotic types that fail to round-trip through the C stream). - Hand-rolled `arrow::ffi_stream` was chosen over the `arrow-pyarrow` crate: arrow-pyarrow 58 requires pyo3 0.28 (this crate is on 0.26), and arrow-pyarrow 57.x pins arrow-array 57 (incompatible with ggsql's arrow-58 `DataFrame` types). A pyo3 upgrade can happen later on its own merits. - Minimum pyarrow is now 15 (the public `RecordBatchReader.from_stream` consumption API landed in 15.0; 14 only has the export side). The `arrow` crate dependency gains its `ffi` feature. - Export direction (`df_to_py`): the `RecordBatch` is wrapped in an `FFI_ArrowArrayStream`, exported as a `PyCapsule` with a C Data Interface-correct destructor, and consumed via a small `#[pyclass]` shim exposing `__arrow_c_stream__()` → `pa.RecordBatchReader.from_stream(...).read_all()`. - Import direction (`py_to_df`, the hot path): `table.__arrow_c_stream__()` → `ArrowArrayStreamReader::from_raw` → `concat_batches`, with the same empty-table semantics as the IPC path. ## Verification - Full test suite passes in both boundary modes: `uv run pytest tests/` with and without `GGSQL_ARROW_IPC=1` (136 passed, 5 skipped in each), including 15 new edge-case/parity tests (dictionary-encoded columns, timestamps with timezones, empty results, chunked multi-batch tables, nullable columns, extension types, IPC-fallback smoke test). - `cargo fmt -- --check` and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` are clean. - Leak smoke test: 200 register+read iterations show flat `ru_maxrss` (Δ ~1 MB). - Boundary microbenchmark (1M rows × 50 cols int64, 5 iterations of register + `SELECT *`; script below, deliberately not committed): zero-copy stream 17.5s / 3246 MB peak RSS vs IPC 99.2s / 4247 MB — ~5.7× faster with ~1 GB lower peak RSS. Note DuckDB ArrowVTab ingestion (2048-row chunks) is a constant cost in both modes; the delta isolates the boundary savings.
Benchmark script (run with uv run python bench_arrow_boundary.py) ```python #!/usr/bin/env python3 """Microbenchmark for the Python<->Rust Arrow boundary. Registers a large pyarrow Table and reads it back through DuckDBReader, exercising py_to_df (register) and df_to_py (execute_sql). Runs the inner benchmark in two subprocesses -- default (zero-copy C stream) and GGSQL_ARROW_IPC=1 (legacy IPC) -- and prints a comparison. Note: DuckDB's ArrowVTab ingestion (chunked at 2048 rows) is a constant cost in both modes; the delta between modes isolates the boundary savings. Usage: uv run python scripts/bench_arrow_boundary.py [--rows N] [--cols N] [--iters N] """ import argparse import os import subprocess import sys INNER = r""" import os import resource import sys import time import pyarrow as pa import ggsql rows, cols, iters = (int(x) for x in sys.argv[1:4]) # ru_maxrss is bytes on macOS, KiB on Linux RSS_UNIT = 1 if sys.platform == "darwin" else 1024 cols_data = {f"c{i}": pa.array(range(rows), type=pa.int64()) for i in range(cols)} table = pa.table(cols_data) reader = ggsql.DuckDBReader("duckdb://memory") # Warmup (also establishes the high-water mark baseline) reader.register("t", table) reader.execute_sql("SELECT * FROM t") start = time.perf_counter() for _ in range(iters): reader.register("t", table, replace=True) out = reader.execute_sql("SELECT * FROM t") elapsed = time.perf_counter() - start mode = "ipc" if os.environ.get("GGSQL_ARROW_IPC") else "stream" peak_mb = resource.getrusage(resource.RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss * RSS_UNIT / 1e6 print(f"RESULT mode={mode} elapsed={elapsed:.3f} peak_rss_mb={peak_mb:.0f} rows_out={out.num_rows}") """ def run_mode(mode: str, rows: int, cols: int, iters: int) -> str: env = dict(os.environ) if mode == "ipc": env["GGSQL_ARROW_IPC"] = "1" else: env.pop("GGSQL_ARROW_IPC", None) proc = subprocess.run( [sys.executable, "-c", INNER, str(rows), str(cols), str(iters)], env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True, ) for line in proc.stdout.splitlines(): if line.startswith("RESULT"): return line raise RuntimeError(f"no RESULT line; stdout={proc.stdout} stderr={proc.stderr}") def main() -> None: parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__) parser.add_argument("--rows", type=int, default=1_000_000) parser.add_argument("--cols", type=int, default=50) parser.add_argument("--iters", type=int, default=5) args = parser.parse_args() print(f"rows={args.rows} cols={args.cols} iters={args.iters}") for mode in ("stream", "ipc"): print(run_mode(mode, args.rows, args.cols, args.iters)) if __name__ == "__main__": main() ```

title: feat: enable spatial (map) support in the Vega-Lite writer
description:
## Summary

Enables the ggsql crate's `spatial` cargo feature so `DRAW spatial` map layers render through the Vega-Lite writer. Today the wheel parses and validates spatial queries, but rendering fails with `Output generation error: Spatial visualization requires the 'spatial' feature to be enabled` — after this change, maps render end to end, including through the `render_chart()` → Altair → browser-widget path.

### Runtime requirement: DuckDB spatial extension

All `DRAW spatial` queries need DuckDB's `spatial` extension at runtime — the reader issues `LOAD spatial` automatically (extent computation uses `ST_` functions) but never `INSTALL` it. So users must run `INSTALL spatial` once per machine (e.g. via `DuckDBReader.execute_sql()`); the ~59 MB download is cached per DuckDB version/platform under `~/.duckdb/extensions`. Without it, spatial queries fail with a clear SQL error pointing at `INSTALL spatial`.

With the extension present, verified working:

- Polygon maps and choropleths from WKB geometry columns or the built-in `ggsql:world` dataset (identity projection, with graticule)
- Named map projections (`PROJECT TO mercator`, `equal_earth`, …) via server-side `ST_Transform`
- Point layers and mixed geometry types in one `spatial` layer
- Faceted small-multiple maps (each panel fits its own extent)

### Binary size impact: negligible

Same crate, same release profile, only the feature toggled: 60,737,888 → 60,871,744 bytes (+134 KB, +0.22%). The feature pulls in only the pure-Rust `geozero` crate (`with-wkb`/`with-wkt`/`with-geojson`) — no native dependencies (no PROJ/GEOS).

Note: `ggsql-r` has the same feature list (plus `odbc`); enabling spatial there is an identical one-line change if parity is wanted, but is out of scope here.

## Verification

```python
import ggsql

reader = ggsql.DuckDBReader("duckdb://memory")
reader.execute_sql("INSTALL spatial")   # one-time per machine; ggsql LOADs automatically after that

spec = reader.execute("VISUALISE FROM ggsql:world DRAW spatial")
vl_json = ggsql.VegaLiteWriter().render(spec)        # geoshape layers + fitted projection
chart = ggsql.VegaLiteWriter().render_chart(spec)    # Altair LayerChart, to_dict() round-trips
```

Tests: `uv run pytest tests/` — new `TestSpatial` class covers Vega-Lite rendering of `DRAW spatial` (basic and choropleth) plus the `render_chart()` Altair round-trip. The class fixture `INSTALL`s the extension (skips when offline); a 10-minute timeout on the CI test step bounds download hangs. Rust checks: `cargo fmt -- --check` and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` are clean.
